pundit.name: Landon Donovan
pundit.take:
**Look, I understand why people see potential in "Ghost Pepper" Devin's roster, but drafting Haiti in the fourth round was like buying fireworks for a rainy day.** I feel for him, truly, because his recent 2-1 win with Spain over Belgium is a glimmer of hope in an otherwise underwhelming strategy. He's sitting in second place with 71 points, but that could just be luck shining down or the cosmic balance correcting itself because, let's face it, Haiti wasn't the universe's best-kept secret. Meanwhile, "The Backpass Assassin" Gayden, with his 39 points and English-centric optimism, is probably betting his entire farm on England pulling something close to a miracle against Norway in Miami Gardens.

When it comes to Norway facing England, real world form suggests an intriguing contest between structured gameplay and whatever Gayden is hoping England will do. Predicting with the most resounding confidence possible, I foresee England tripping over their own boots while Norway, with all their Scandinavian charm, gracefully navigates the field. But hey, credit to Gayden for trying! Maybe England will surprise us all and decide today is the day that good karma finally cycles back to one perennially drafted team.
